green-deep.displayName: Green Deep (AA green text/links on light, 6.13:1)
green-deep.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #009260, #06140d 26%). The written form of the lead colour: links, .accent, ol folios, ledger figures, the Fig. mark, the printed folio. Small green text is never set in the raw corporate hex.

green-field.displayName: Green Field (the divider plane, 4.95:1 against Paper)
green-field.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #009260, #04140d 14%). The full-bleed .section plane — the bright register. A divider never paints raw #009260.

green-wash.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #009260, paper 90%). The palest ground in the system: the highlighted code line and the filled .depth row. At 90% Paper it resolves to oklch(0.950 0.014 241) — a cool near-white that reads as a marked row, not as a green tint.

navy-field.displayName: Navy Field (the deep pole plane, 13.10:1 against Paper)
navy-field.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #00268a, #03081c 8%). The .closing colophon and the .section.navy divider — the surface the deep register measures against.

navy-deep.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #00268a, #04060f 30%). --ond-mark-ink on the deep pole: text and glyphs sitting ON gold. Also the navy duotone plate ground.

gold-bright.displayName: Gold Bright (the deep pole's mark, 7.13:1 on navy)
gold-bright.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #cca352, white 24%). What --ond-mark resolves to on .section.navy, .closing and .media: plate rules, dark-field ticks, the closing kicker, the on-dark folio. Never reached by hand and never on a bright field (2.71:1 on green).

brown-deep.displayName: Brown Deep (AA brown small text on light, 7.76:1)
brown-deep.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #d57912, #140a02 44%). The .kicker.warm / .callout.warm voice and the .step-vec chip; the written form of the counter-thread.

warm-field.displayName: Warm Field (the stakes divider, 5.71:1 against Paper)
warm-field.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, #d57912, #160b02 30%). The .section.warm plane — the second bright field, used sparingly for the critical-stakes strand.

browser-dot.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, ink-faint, paper 25%), mixed inline in 05-embeds-code.css:89-92 — the three 0.6rem dots in the .chrome / .site-frame bar. Not a hairline and not text: the one grey that represents a browser rather than drawing the page. One user; not a :root token.

code-title-blue.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, navy, sky 18%), mixed inline in 05-embeds-code.css:26. The only place Sky is spent: it lifts a function or title token off the keyword navy without adding a hue. One user.

scroll-thumb.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, green, paper 18%), mixed inline in 05-embeds-code.css:48 for the .scroll-panel webkit thumb (11px track, 3px Sunken inset, pill radius). Lightened so browser furniture does not read as the lead colour; Firefox's scrollbar-color takes --green directly. One user.

gold-wash.purpose: color-mix(in oklch, gold, white 18%), mixed inline in the mark / .hl gradient (01-foundations.css:423). Close to gold-bright but measured on Paper rather than on the deep pole, which is why the two values differ. One user.

scrim-ink.purpose: oklch(0.14 0.02 258), the base colour of every .media-scrim stop and of the theme-owned footer band (03-layouts.css:192-202); the lightbox backdrop mixes to within two channels of it (05-embeds-code.css:180). Deeper than Rule on purpose — it has to hold Paper at 13.2:1 over a worst-case white photograph. The TOC overlay's oklch(0.16 0.012 258) and the graphite viewport frame both land on Rule and are not separate values.

capture-letterbox.purpose: The literal behind an app screenshot of any aspect ratio (.demo-shot-view, 05-embeds-code.css:161). Deliberately outside the cool ink ramp: it belongs to the captured artifact, like the browser chrome around it, not to the page's own neutrals. One user.

duo-ground.purpose: The literal ink-green backing every documentary plate is duotoned onto — the deepest surface in the system and the reason .media sits in the deep register.

ink-faint.displayName: Ink Faint (5.15:1 on paper, 4.51:1 on sunken)

display.purpose: Cover titles (5.30rem), section-divider titles (6.10rem), statements (5.60rem). Libre Franklin at 700, line-height <= 0.98, tracking -0.018em. The LOUD voice. Only the stat and metric numerals (9.50rem --fs-mega) stay at 800.

headline.purpose: The standard h2.slide-title under the 4px green marker bar: 700, 3.50rem, --track-tight -0.012em, max-width 22ch.

title.purpose: Sub-headings and column heads; Libre Franklin 700.

lead.purpose: The serif lead paragraph, max-width 30ch; also h4, which deliberately stays in the serif register.

body.purpose: EB Garamond prose at 1.52rem — deliberately large for hall projection; max-width 62ch. The QUIET counter-voice.

label.purpose: Every in-canvas label that carries meaning: kickers, callout labels, stat labels, column heads, chart heads, bar-axis ticks, table headers, chips, figure numbers, step numbers, evidence terms. 1.15rem --fs-label, --track-case 0.005em, SENTENCE CASE (authors type it so). Tracked uppercase belongs to the chrome alone.

chrome.purpose: The only uppercase voice, and only outside the reading canvas: the running head (0.22em), the footer title, the TOC button and eyebrow, the .site-qr label, the print Excerpt band and the .pdf-imprint. 0.80rem --fs-footer, --track-label 0.18em. The theme's seven text-transform: uppercase rules are all here.

mono.purpose: The third face, a utility rather than a voice: it never carries prose. Code blocks (1.02rem measured), the scroll-panel excerpt, frame-bar and QR URLs, and document references. Vendored by tools/fetch-fonts.py, italic subset included because highlight.js sets comments in it. No tracking, never uppercase.

shadows.name: shadow-2
shadows.purpose: The captured or borrowed artifact floating over the page, and only these four: the browser-chrome screenshot frame (.chrome), the live embed in the same chrome (.site-frame), the demo capture (.demo-shot), and the QR that pops over a frame (.site-qr).

shadows.name: shadow-pop
shadows.purpose: True modal overlays only: the TOC panel and the lightbox image. The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule.

shadows.name: scroll-inset
shadows.purpose: Not a token: written inline on .scroll-panel (05-embeds-code.css:42) and the only inset shadow in the theme. It darkens into the panel from the top edge to mark that the file is cut off above — the affordance that let the panel drop its border. Inset, so it adds no elevation and does not breach the Overlay-Only Shadow Rule.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Ease-out-quint; the default easing for all transitions and the draw animations.

motion.name: dur
motion.purpose: Default state-transition duration (links, buttons, TOC items, fragments).

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: The drawn half of the ink-on-paper signature: the title marker bar, the section and closing plate rules and the share-bar fill draw in from the left on one rule-draw scaleX keyframe; chart bars grow from the baseline, the one animation left on the layout path so each bar's numeral rides up with it.

motion.name: count
motion.purpose: The counted third movement: [data-count] numerals roll up on slide entry, run by deck.js. Longer than --draw on purpose - a numeral needs legible frames to read as counting.

motion.name: draw-run
motion.purpose: The one stiller. Every signature animation takes its duration from here, and print, the ?print-pdf preview, prefers-reduced-motion, the scroll view (.reveal-viewport.reveal-scroll .reveal) and .no-draw (deck or slide) each set it to 0s rather than restating the animated marks; deck.js reads the same property off the slide before starting a count. The scroll view needs it because reveal adds and removes .present at every scroll trigger, in both directions.

breakpoints.name: chrome-compact
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: chrome outside the scaled canvas compacts (runhead hidden, footer title dropped, --slide-pad-x down to 1.6rem). Slide content itself never responds — the 1280x720 canvas scales uniformly.

breakpoints.name: shallow-screen
breakpoints.purpose: max-height: a real footer strip (--footer-reserve 2.4rem) is reserved outside the area reveal scales into, so the footer never covers content on landscape phones. The scroll view does not shorten .reveal, so its fixed band falls below the fold here — a known, documented gap.

breakpoints.name: scroll-activation
breakpoints.purpose: Not a breakpoint by decision: reveal's automatic scroll-view switch (scrollActivationWidth) is disabled in the engine config, because the automatic mobile switch at <=435px clipped two-column slides on portrait phones. The scroll view is reached only by ?view=scroll / ?view=reader.

print.name: excerpt-mark
print.purpose: Draws the paper cut on .scroll-panel: a fade into the Sunken fill plus a ruled Excerpt band (Extrait under html[lang=fr]; the address appended when the panel carries data-source-url). Set to block by @media print and by html.reveal-print for the ?print-pdf preview.

print.name: scroll-hint-display
print.purpose: Suppresses the on-screen scroll instruction in print, where it would be a false one. Declared alongside --excerpt-mark in the same two paper contexts.

runtimeContracts.print: Ordinary pages use border-box block flow; heroes retain flex centring. Fit with layout zoom after media settles and before pagination; verify bounds, imprints and rendered PDF pages.
runtimeContracts.media: Live frames show directly; no opt-in control. A frame without its own fallback gets an engine notice (div.frame-fallback[data-frame-notice], 'Loading the site...') that hides once a no-cors reachability request succeeds and otherwise becomes the unavailable notice with a persistent Open link (offline, blocked or 8 s). An authored img.frame-fallback stays until the origin/source-checked data-ready-message arrives, or data-frame-trusted is empty or equals location.origin and the site is reachable. .site-frame-open always opens a new tab (audit). Lazy gallery media resolves before display.
runtimeContracts.motion: Reduced motion disables Auto-Animate geometry changes and signature effects; opacity/colour feedback remains.
runtimeContracts.sharing: Footer stroke-icon button copies semantic slide URL and announces success; explicit authored IDs survive title edits.
runtimeContracts.chrome: One overline per slide: the running head is hidden on hero slides and on any slide carrying a .kicker or .dateline (update() in 03-toc-sync.js).

components.name: Print Imprint (per-page folio)
components.description: PDF-only page footer. The live deck footer and running head are hidden under html.reveal-print; buildPrintImprints() appends one imprint per .pdf-page, numbered from that page's own index. Its rule matches .deck-footer::before exactly (2px, Rule) so the two read as one device. Dark pages invert through the same on-dark tokens and the same two registers as the screen chrome, via the shared fieldOf() helper — and because the imprint is a sibling of the section rather than a descendant, it must be named in the deep-register override list to reach the deep ramp, exactly as .deck-footer is.

components.css: .ds-plate { margin: 0; max-width: 30rem; } .ds-plate-img { height: 11rem; background: #04140d; border: 1px solid oklch(0.623 0.010 256); background-image: linear-gradient(135deg, #04140d 0%, color-mix(in oklch, #009260, #04140d 40%) 60%, color-mix(in oklch, #009260, #04140d 14%) 100%); } .ds-plate-cap { display: flex; gap: 0.7em; margin-top: 0.55em; padding-top: 0.5em; border-top: 2px solid oklch(0.165 0.014 258); } .ds-fig-no { flex: none; font-family: 'Libre Franklin', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 800; font-size: 1.15rem; letter-spacing: 0.005em; color: color-mix(in oklch, #009260, #06140d 26%); } .ds-fig-cap { font-family: 'EB Garamond', Georgia, serif; font-style: italic; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.34; color: oklch(0.405 0.018 258); }

components.css: .ds-media { --ond-mark: color-mix(in oklch, #cca352, white 24%); position: relative; height: 20rem; background: linear-gradient(120deg, #6b6f74, #cfd3d6); overflow: hidden; } .ds-media-scrim { position: absolute; inset: 0; background: linear-gradient(0deg, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.94) 0%, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.86) 30%, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.52) 54%, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.12) 74%, transparent 86%), linear-gradient(90deg, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.84) 0%, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.48) 44%, transparent 76%); } .ds-media-band { position: absolute; left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0; height: 4rem; pointer-events: none; background: linear-gradient(0deg, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.94) 0%, oklch(0.14 0.02 258 / 0.86) 62%, transparent 100%); } .ds-media-caption { position: absolute; left: 4.8rem; right: 4.8rem; bottom: 4.5rem; z-index: 2; max-width: 34ch; } .ds-media-kicker { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.15rem; letter-spacing: 0.005em; color: var(--ond-mark); margin: 0 0 0.5rem; } .ds-media-title { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 2.6rem; line-height: 0.98; letter-spacing: -0.012em; color: oklch(0.991 0.001 250); margin: 0; }

components.css: .ds-flow { display: flex; align-items: stretch; gap: 2rem; } .ds-flow-step { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 0.4em; border-top: 4px solid var(--rule, oklch(0.165 0.014 258)); padding: 0.75rem 0 0; } .ds-step-n { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.15rem; letter-spacing: 0.005em; color: var(--navy, #00268a); } .ds-step-h { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 1.52rem; line-height: 1.08; color: var(--ink, oklch(0.205 0.016 258)); } .ds-flow-step p { margin: 0; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--ink-soft, oklch(0.405 0.018 258)); } .ds-step-vec { align-self: flex-start; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 1rem; color: var(--brown-deep, #8a4c05); background: var(--sunken, oklch(0.945 0.004 250)); border: none; border-radius: 3px; padding: 0.2em 0.5em; } .ds-flow-arrow { flex: none; align-self: flex-start; display: flex; align-items: center; height: 4px; margin-top: -1.5px; color: var(--green-deep, #00713f); font-weight: 700; font-size: 1.18rem; }

components.name: Ruled Table
components.description: A ledger, not a grid: sentence-case gothic headers at the label size over a near-black rule, hairlines between rows, striped even rows, and one gutter measured against the table's own font-size.
components.css: .ds-table { border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%; font-size: 1.18rem; font-family: 'EB Garamond', Georgia, serif; color: var(--ink, oklch(0.205 0.016 258)); } .ds-table th, .ds-table td { text-align: left; padding: 0.55em calc(0.9 * 1.18rem); border: none; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, oklch(0.744 0.005 250)); } .ds-table th { font-family: 'Libre Franklin', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.15rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.005em; color: var(--ink-bold, oklch(0.15 0.016 262)); border-bottom: 3px solid var(--rule, oklch(0.165 0.014 258)); } .ds-table tbody tr:nth-child(even) { background: color-mix(in oklch, var(--sunken, oklch(0.945 0.004 250)), transparent 30%); } .ds-table .ds-num { text-align: right; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums; }

narrative.overview: Broadsheet is the visual system of a reveal.js engine for academic talks: an authored scholarly broadsheet, not a slide template. Three ideas carry it. An inverted type hierarchy: the newspaper gothic (Libre Franklin, bold at 700, lightly negative-tracked) is the loud display voice and the humanist book serif (EB Garamond) the quiet voice for prose, leads and quotations. Colour is a field, not a sprinkle: the six binding Bayreuth corporate colours are spent as flat structural planes and heavy rules. A crisp, high-contrast page: near-black ink on a cool near-white, structure drawn by 3-4px rules rather than boxes. The voice is authored by a historian and must not read as template-made or AI-generated: one overline per slide, sentence-case labels inside the canvas, ornaments used sparingly, the institution logo as an affiliation after the byline. WCAG 2.2 AA is binding and hall legibility leads every sizing decision. Narrative history and superseded values live in docs/design-history.md. A ZMO brand skin (shared/brands/zmo/) re-dresses the same engine as the ZMO PowerPoint and is governed by its own section, not by these rules.
keyCharacteristics: Inverted type hierarchy: loud gothic display at 700, quiet serif prose
Colour as full-bleed structural fields (green leads, navy is the deep pole, gold sparks the deep pole only)
Two on-dark registers, split by measured luminance: the deep pole re-opens a tonal ramp and takes gold; the bright fields spend Paper and separate their tiers by weight
One signature mark: a 4px green marker bar above every standard slide title
One overline per slide; sentence-case labels inside the canvas, uppercase only in the chrome
Ruled, not boxed: hairlines and heavy editorial rules instead of cards
Flat by default; shadows only on true overlays
"Ink on paper" motion: rules draw in, bars grow, figures count up; one switch (`--draw-run`) stills all three

rules.name: The Field, Not Sprinkle Rule
rules.body: Colour arrives as a flat plane, a heavy bar or a solid fill, or not at all; never as a tint, gradient wash or scattered accent.

rules.name: The One Gold Spark Rule
rules.body: Gold reaches a dark field only through `--ond-mark` where it resolves to gold-bright. Never a second accent on a light slide, never hand-placed on a bright field.

rules.name: The Two Dark Registers Rule
rules.body: Nothing on a dark field is coloured by hand: six on-dark tokens (`--ond-text`, `--ond-quiet`, `--ond-chrome`, `--ond-mark`, `--ond-rule`, `--ond-mark-ink`) hold the colours, and their `:root` values are the bright register.

rules.name: The Inverted Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: h1–h3 are Libre Franklin 700 with negative tracking; prose, leads, quotations and captions are EB Garamond. Never swap them.

rules.name: The Serif h4 Rule
rules.body: `h4` stays in the serif: an emphatic lead, not a label.

rules.name: The Hall Label Rule
rules.body: Labels split by distance, not by component. A label inside the canvas that says what a figure counts, which decade a bar sits in or what a column holds is set at `--fs-label` in sentence case with `--track-case`, and the author types it in sentence case. Tracked uppercase is chrome only: the theme's seven `text-transform: uppercase` rules are all chrome. `--track-hall` (0.10em) survives only for per-deck CSS. Test: cover the numerals and read the labels from the back of the room.

rules.name: The One Overline Rule
rules.body: A slide carries at most one line above its title. The engine's running head names the section on content slides; a slide with a `.kicker` or `.dateline` hides it (`update()` in `03-toc-sync.js`), and heroes never show it. The kicker has no tick: the title marker is the slide's one mark. Add a kicker only when this slide needs a label the running head cannot give.

rules.name: The Third Face Is Pinned Too
rules.body: `tools/fetch-fonts.py` vendors JetBrains Mono, italic included because highlight.js sets comments in it. The rest of the stack is a fallback for a failed load, not a choice.

rules.name: The Fixed Canvas Rule
rules.body: No vw, vh or `clamp()` for slide content; figures and code cap at `--block-max-h` (28rem). The sanctioned viewport units are on true overlays only: the TOC panel (`90vh`) and the lightbox (`88vh` / `80vh`).

rules.name: The Floating Control Clearance Rule
rules.body: A control floating over a panel insets the panel's text by its box plus a gap; the rule beneath stays full width (`.toc-head { padding-right: calc(2.4rem + var(--space-sm)) }`).

rules.name: The Chrome Is Not Prose Rule
rules.body: Furniture inside `.reveal` states its own list, measure and marker at `.reveal`-qualified specificity (`.reveal .toc-list`).

rules.name: The Border-Box Chrome Rule
rules.body: Chrome that declares a width against the viewport sets `box-sizing: border-box` in the same rule; only the canvas has it.

rules.name: The Overlay-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: An outer shadow only on an element that floats above the deck; never on callouts, stats, panels, columns or other in-flow content.

rules.name: The Ruled, Not Boxed Rule
rules.body: Rules open, hairlines divide, a left bar marks the active choice. The only surface is the flat Sunken inset (`.panel.sunken`, `.reveal pre`, `.scroll-panel`), with no border. `.flow-step` and `.panel` open on the same 4px (`--bar`) Rule and are separated by the gutter.

rules.name: One run, one opening rule
rules.body: In a run of callouts only the first opens on the 3px rule; `.callout + .callout` takes a hairline.

rules.name: The Rule Opens From Above Rule
rules.body: A heavy opening rule needs air above it (`.marginnote`: `margin-top: var(--space-lg)`, 0 as a first child).

rules.name: The Rules Line Up Or Clearly Don't Rule
rules.body: Adjacent copies of one device end at the same x or differ obviously: `.stat-grid + .callout` takes the ledger's column width, while a standalone callout keeps 60ch.

rules.name: The Ink-on-Paper Motion Rule
rules.body: `--draw: 560ms`, ease-out-quint: rules draw in from the left, chart bars grow, figures count up (`--count: 900ms`). One keyframe, `rule-draw` (`scaleX`), serves three marks (title marker, section and closing plate rules) and the share-bar fill. Only the column chart animates a layout property (`height`), so each numeral rides its bar.

rules.name: The One Stiller Rule
rules.body: Every signature animation takes its duration from `--draw-run`; print, `?print-pdf`, reduced motion, the scroll view and `.no-draw` set it to `0s`. `deck.js` reads it before a count and skips counts in a hidden tab; `tools/browser-check.mjs` proves the switch reaches every mark.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Keeps The Feedback Rule
rules.body: Under reduced motion every displacement goes; colour and opacity changes keep their authored timing.

rules.name: The Themed Focus Rule
rules.body: `--focus-ring` is `--green` on light and Paper on dark fields, with a `var(--radius-sm)` corner on `.deck-btn`, `.toc-item`, `.is-zoomable` and in-slide links.

rules.name: The Focus Ring Is Not Animated Rule
rules.body: Every transition names its properties; `transition: all` appears nowhere. `.reveal .fragment` restates reveal's `transition: all` as `opacity, color, transform, visibility`.

rules.name: The Inline Style Wins Rule
rules.body: Before overriding a vendor property, check whether the vendor sets it inline (the `.reveal-viewport` cross-fade needs `!important`).

rules.name: The Two Image Treatments Rule
rules.body: Every image is a duotone plate with a ruled caption or a true-colour capture in browser chrome. No naked JPEGs.

rules.name: The One Bar Rule
rules.body: `.site-frame-bar, .chrome-bar` is one device declared once in `05-embeds-code.css`; it neutralises caption styling so it spans the frame whatever element carries it. Only the Open link is the live frame's own.

rules.name: The Padding Measures The Container Rule
rules.body: A gutter that must align across type sizes is measured against the container, not each cell's em.

rules.name: The Paper Cannot Scroll Rule
rules.body: A `.scroll-panel` prints what fits, fades into Sunken, closes on the heavy rule and carries an `Excerpt` band (`Extrait` in French) naming its `data-source-url`. `--excerpt-mark` and `--scroll-hint-display` are set for `@media print` and the `?print-pdf` preview.

rules.name: The Scrim Guarantee Rule
rules.body: A dark ground the theme does not own is manufactured; a new overlay-on-image pattern states its contrast against a worst-case white frame.

dos: **Do** put the green marker above every standard title.
**Do** spend colour as fields and use the deep variants for small text.
**Do** colour dark fields through the on-dark tokens and `fieldOf()`.
**Do** keep display at 700 and `h4` in the serif.
**Do** type labels in sentence case and give a slide one overline at most.
**Do** centre heroes with the seven classes and add a new one to all three lists.
**Do** open steps and panels on the 4px rule with air above.
**Do** name every transitioned property and still motion through `--draw-run`.
**Do** show live sites directly with a saved view and a new-tab Open link.
**Do** step a list with `.fragment` only when the room should be walked through it.
donts: **Don't** shadow in-flow content or border the Sunken inset.
**Don't** use viewport units in the canvas.
**Don't** build chrome from author strings without `escapeHTML()`.
**Don't** put gold on a light slide or gold, amber or sky on a bright field.
**Don't** carry a large form on a low-opacity fill.
**Don't** waive the fit check with boilerplate or widen `.lead` past 30ch outside `.closing`.
**Don't** write `transition: all` or zero every duration for reduced motion.
**Don't** leave an instruction in print the reader cannot follow.
**Don't** reach for an ornament on an ordinary slide.
**Don't** convert the OKLCH neutrals or "correct" the corporate hex.
